- When sentiment turns bullish sharply (e.g., +1.00 jump), model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if sentiment spike is >0.67.
- If sentiment turns bearish after a rally (e.g., -1.00 or -0.67), model often undercorrects — add 2–5% to forecast to account for mean reversion.
- High news volume (>3.0) correlates with overestimation — apply 3–7% downward adjustment if news volume >3 and forecast >true outcome.
- If last 3–5 days show strong upward momentum (sentiment >0.67), model often fails to capture continuation — extend forecast slightly higher, but cap at +10% above recent high.
- If sentiment is flat or negative for 3+ days, model tends to lag — forecast should be 1–3% above recent low to avoid underestimating rebound.
- Model consistently underestimates true outcomes when sentiment is positive but news volume is low — increase forecast by 2–5% if sentiment >0.67 and news volume <2.0.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes are common — if forecast > true outcome by >5%, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment remains bullish.
- If sentiment is negative for 2+ days, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 3–7% to avoid overbought bias.
- Forecast should be adjusted downward if sentiment change is negative and news volume is high — reduce by 2–5% if sentiment change <0 and news volume >3.0.
- Model tends to underestimate true outcomes when sentiment is positive but recent price is rising — add 3–7% to forecast if sentiment >0.67 and price is trending up.
